skill.name: grill-with-docs
skill.description: A guided interview that tests a plan or design and creates ADRs and glossary entries as decisions emerge.
skill.summary: Runs a rigorous planning interview and records decisions, assumptions, and domain terms.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by Markdown backticks around a slash command in SKILL.md line 7. The skill contains prompt instructions only and no executable code, network access, file writes, secret access, or prompt injection language. No semantic security findings were identified.

static_findings.snippet: Run a `/grilling` session, using the `/domain-modeling` skill.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 7 uses Markdown backticks to format the /grilling and /domain-modeling slash command names. There is no Ruby or shell execution context, interpolation, or executable code.

content.value_statement: Design plans often hide weak assumptions and unclear terms. This skill runs a focused interview and turns the discussion into ADR and glossary notes.
actual_capabilities: Runs a grilling session to question a plan or design.
Uses the domain-modeling skill as part of the workflow.
Supports ADR creation during the discussion.
Supports glossary creation as terms emerge.
Frames the workflow as an interview for design refinement.
limitations: It depends on the separate /grilling and /domain-modeling skills being available.
It does not include executable scripts or automation logic.
It cannot validate facts beyond the context supplied by the user.
It does not define a document storage location or file format.

use_cases.title: Review Architecture Direction
use_cases.description: Pressure test a proposed architecture and capture decisions as ADR notes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Implementation Plans
use_cases.description: Question a feature plan before coding and identify unclear assumptions.

use_cases.title: Build Shared Vocabulary
use_cases.description: Turn debated domain terms into a glossary during design discussion.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Plan Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a /grilling session on this feature plan. Ask direct questions and capture decisions as ADR notes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single feature plan.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify Domain Terms
prompt_templates.prompt: Use /grilling with /domain-modeling. Challenge unclear business terms and build a glossary from agreed definitions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review when terminology is disputed.

prompt_templates.title: Stress Test a Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Interview me about this design proposal. Identify weak assumptions, missing tradeoffs, and decisions that need ADR entries.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before a design is approved.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Decision Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a rigorous grilling session before architecture review. Produce concise ADR candidates, unresolved questions, and glossary updates from the discussion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced preparation for a formal decision meeting.

output_examples.input: A team wants to choose a job queue design before implementation.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks targeted questions, records a draft ADR, and lists unresolved queue ownership terms.

output_examples.input: A product team has conflicting names for the same customer concept.
output_examples.output: The assistant challenges each definition and produces glossary entries for agreed terms.

output_examples.input: A technical lead wants a final review before sharing a design proposal.
output_examples.output: The assistant surfaces tradeoffs, missing evidence, and ADR candidates for human approval.

best_practices: Bring a concrete plan, design, or decision draft before starting the session.
Answer questions with evidence, constraints, and ownership details.
Review generated ADR and glossary notes before sharing them.
anti_patterns: Using the skill with only a vague idea or missing context.
Treating draft ADR notes as approved decisions without review.
Skipping domain modeling when terminology is disputed.

faq.question: Does this skill run code?
faq.answer: No. It is prompt-only and contains no executable scripts.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: It lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it require other skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It references /grilling and /domain-modeling for the workflow.

faq.question: Can it create final ADRs?
faq.answer: It helps draft ADR content. A human should review and approve decisions.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when a plan needs pressure testing before approval or implementation.

faq.question: Can it maintain a glossary?
faq.answer: It can help capture terms and definitions during the session.
